extracted.intended_audience: owners and operators of CCR facilities, state and tribal regulators, environmental consultants, and other stakeholders involved in CCR unit management and compliance
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and evaluation criteria for legacy coal combustion residual (CCR) surface impoundments and CCR management units (CCRMU), including closure, post-closure care, recordkeeping, website posting, facility evaluation, and groundwater monitoring/corrective action expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description of final cover system and performance
rubrics_metrics.description: The closure plan must include a description of the final cover system and how the final cover system will achieve the regulatory performance standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the base of the impoundment intersects with groundwater, the closure plan must discuss engineering measures taken to ensure that the groundwater had been removed from the unit prior to the start of installing the final cover system, as required by §257.102(d)(2)(i). The plan must also describe how the facility plans to meet the requirements in §257.102(d)(1) to “control, minimize or eliminate, to the maximum extent feasible, post-closure infiltration of liquids into the waste and releases of CCR, leachate, or contaminated run-off to the ground or surface waters.” This could include, for example, the installation of engineering controls that would address post-closure infiltration of liquids into the waste from all directions, as well as any post-closure releases to the groundwater from the sides and bottom of the unit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation of a written P.E.-certified post-closure care plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners or operators of legacy CCR surface impoundments must prepare a written post-closure plan certified by a professional engineer per §257.104(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA finalized a deadline of no later than Monday, November 8, 2027 (36 months from the effective date) to comply with the post-closure care requirement in §257.104(d) (codified at §257.100(f)(5)(ii)). The contents of the P.E.-certified plan are stated in §257.104(d)(1)(i) through (iii) and can be summarized as: a description of the monitoring and maintenance activities required for the unit, the frequency that these activities will be performed, information for the point-of-contact during the post-closure care period, and planned uses of the property.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadline to complete closure and allowable extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners or operators of legacy CCR surface impoundments must complete closure activities within the time frames in §257.102(f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 257.102(f) generally requires completion of closure within five years from initiating closure. The regulations establish conditions and documentation requirements under which owners or operators can demonstrate and receive two-year extensions. For CCR surface impoundments of 40 acres or less, the deadline can only be extended by one two-year extension. For CCR surface impoundments larger than 40 acres, the deadline can be extended in increments of two years for no more than five times.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-closure care duration and activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-closure care requires monitoring and maintenance of units that have closed with CCR in place for at least 30 years after closure completion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During this post-closure period, the facility is required to continue groundwater monitoring and corrective action, where necessary, consistent with §257.104.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping requirements for legacy CCR surface impoundments
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners or operators must comply with recordkeeping requirements in §§257.105 through 257.107 and maintain required information in the facility operating record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The CCR regulations require recording specific information, maintaining files of demonstrations, plans, notifications, and reports that support rule implementation and compliance. Each required file must be maintained in the operating record for the entirety of the retention period specified in §257.105 following submittal and must indicate the date the file was placed in the operating record. Files are required to be submitted into the operating record at the time the documentation becomes available or by the compliance deadline specified in the CCR regulations. Section 257.105 contains a comprehensive listing of each recordkeeping requirement and corresponding retention periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: CCR website posting and internet availability requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners or operators of legacy CCR surface impoundments must maintain a publicly accessible CCR website titled “CCR Rule Compliance Data and Information” to host compliance information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information posted to the publicly accessible internet site must be available for a period of no less than five years from the initial posting date for each submission. Posting must be completed no later than 30 days from submittal of the information to the operating record. Owners or operators have 30 days from the effective date of this rule to establish the CCR website and post required applicable information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public participation and engagement mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule provides mechanisms for public participation but does not add new mandatory public meeting requirements beyond current provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Current regulations require owner/operators to hold a public meeting as part of the assessment of corrective measures in §257.96, create a mechanism for the public to file dust complaints in §257.80(b), and require a 'contact us' form or specific email address on facilities' public CCR websites per §257.107(a). EPA encourages facilities to engage with the public and solicit/incorporate public input into decisions (e.g., closure methods) as able and appropriate, but declined to require additional mandatory public meetings, standardized reporting formats, or owner/operator certification of compliance documents absent evidence those measures are necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification and facility evaluation of CCR management units (CCRMU)
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners or operators of covered CCR facilities must conduct a facility evaluation to identify and delineate any CCRMU containing one ton or more and document the findings in two reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA defines CCRMU to include CCR surface impoundments and landfills closed prior to the 2015 CCR Rule and inactive CCR landfills or piles at covered facilities. The evaluation and reporting requirement applies to facilities currently regulated under the 2015 CCR Rule, inactive facilities with a legacy CCR surface impoundment, and certain facilities that produced electricity for the grid on or after October 19, 2015 but were not regulated in 2015.

rubrics_metrics.name: CCRMU compliance thresholds for 1,000 tons or more
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners or operators must ensure that all identified CCRMU containing 1,000 tons or more comply with existing requirements in 40 CFR part 257, subpart D.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compliance includes groundwater monitoring, corrective action (where necessary), and in certain cases, closure and post-closure care requirements. EPA expects units meeting the 1,000-ton threshold to be subject to these existing subpart D provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration and use of damage cases in regulatory decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA will consider both proven and potential damage cases (documented instances of danger from surface runoff or leachate) as relevant evidence when evaluating risks and developing CCR requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Damage cases provide direct evidence of the extent and nature of risks from actual waste management practices and informed EPA's identification of additional Appendix IV constituents in the 2015 CCR rule. EPA treats both contamination that has migrated off-site and contamination limited to on-site groundwater as relevant; the absence of current receptors does not justify disregarding damage cases. Damage cases are used to evaluate frequency of leaching, management practices that caused leaks, contaminant levels, and nature of impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative Source Demonstration (ASD) and corrective action timing
rubrics_metrics.description: When a facility determines there is a statistically significant increase (SSI) or a statistically significant level (SSL) at a downgradient monitoring well, existing CCR regulations allow the facility an opportunity to complete an ASD attributing the detection to a source other than the regulated unit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For SSLs, if a successful ASD is not completed within 90 days, corrective action must be initiated (see 40 CFR 257.95(g)(3)). For SSIs related to Appendix III constituents, ASD procedures are available under 40 CFR 257.94(e)(2). EPA reviewed ASDs and ACMs on facility websites and identified instances where Federally unregulated CCR sources were claimed as responsible for SSIs/SSLs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of facility documents and data used to identify risks and damage cases
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA used multiple types of publicly available facility documents to review potential damage cases and CCRMU characteristics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents reviewed included groundwater monitoring reports, assessment of corrective measures reports, corrective measures progress reports, remedy selection reports, history of construction reports, closure plans and reports, and fugitive dust control plans (from facilities' CCR websites for 2018–2021). Facilities should be aware these documents are considered in EPA's assessments and may be relied upon in rulemaking records.
